lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON.

instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Tell me which of my recordings a passage of my transcript archive comes from, given the line numbers it was cited by", and give it ranges (Line ranges, first-last: a list, or one string with spaces between them.).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:name-the-recording-behind-transcript-lines and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Reads an archive index the person let this tool read (a JSON list of windows, each with an id, the recording's title, the first and last line it covers and its text) and, for each line range given, lists every window that overlaps it: the window id, the recording's title, the window's line span and its first words.
4. It reads and writes only its own rows through the records door: record:setting (records:read).

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
